label: Glassflow
Window buttons
Enable macOS-style traffic lights *Replaces the window controls with round glass buttons. Turn OFF Arc 2.0's own 'macOS style buttons' first, or the two mods fight over layout.*
Position *Which end of the sidebar row the buttons sit on. Set explicitly, so it does not depend on zen.view.experimental-force-window-controls-left.*
Show colour at rest *On: always tinted. Off: neutral grey until hovered, which is how Arc behaves.*
Stretch into a vertical oval on hover *Only the button under the cursor stretches, not the whole group. Height animates, so nothing around it reflows.*
Oval height multiplier *How far the hovered button stretches, as a multiple of its diameter. 1.0 stays circular, 1.3 is a soft oval, above about 1.8 looks like a capsule.*
Show glyphs on hover *Fades in the close, minimise and maximise marks. Triggered by hovering anywhere in the group, matching macOS, rather than per button.*
Glyph size *How much of the button the mark fills, as a percentage. 76% is close to macOS. Above about 85% the mark starts touching the rim.*

Close colour *Purple by default: destructive, but softer than red. Any CSS colour works. Alpha below about 0.7 is what makes it read as glass rather than paint, and hovering stacks a second pass of this same colour to deepen it.*
Minimise colour *Blue by default, which reads as 'send away'. Keep alpha below about 0.7 or the glass effect disappears.*
Maximise colour *Green by default, the colour macOS already uses for zoom. Keep alpha below about 0.7.*
Diameter *Resting size. macOS uses 12px, Arc uses 14px.*
Gap between buttons *Horizontal spacing. macOS uses roughly 8px.*
Glassy tabs

Enable glassy tinted tabs *Tints tabs with the container or workspace colour. Covers regular, pinned and Essentials tabs. Painted as a background-image so it stacks above Arc's tab colours instead of fighting them.*

Colour source *Container colour is per tab, so tabs in different containers read differently at a glance. Workspace colour is uniform and shifts when you switch spaces. Requires containers or workspace colours to actually be assigned.*

Hide Arc's container glow *Arc paints a blurred bar of container colour across the left half of every container tab. With Zen set to force a container per workspace, that lands on every tab. Glassflow tints the whole tab instead, so this is usually the extra colour you are seeing on the left. Only affects Arc 2.0.*
Selected tab tint *How much colour the active tab carries. Keep well above the unselected value or the two states stop being distinguishable at a glance. Try 20% for subtle, 60% for bold.*
Unselected tab tint *Background tabs. Above roughly 20% these start competing with the selected tab. For subtle tints everywhere, use the accent bar instead.*
Hover tint *Applied to background tabs under the cursor. Sits between the unselected and selected values.*
Gradient direction *How the colour fades across the selected tab. Horizontal reads as depth, vertical as sheen. Reversed directions are useful when the sidebar sits on the right.*

Reverse the gradient on unloaded tabs *Tabs that have not been loaded this session run their gradient the opposite way, so dormant tabs are readable at a glance without dimming them. Has no visible effect when the direction is set to flat.*

Gradient across the whole tab strip *A separate wash behind every tab, spanning the full strip rather than each tab individually. Also gives the frosted blur something with structure to work against. Uses the workspace colour, since container colour only exists per tab.*
Strip gradient strength *How strong the full-strip wash is at its top. Only applies when the strip gradient is on.*

Frosted blur *Blurs whatever sits behind the tab. It can only blur what the browser itself painted, so over a flat sidebar there is little to work with and the effect stays subtle. A compositor pass per tab, so turn this off first if scrolling feels heavy.*
Blur strength *Only applies when frosted blur is on. Larger values smear high-contrast content behind the tab into visible streaks.*
Glass rim *A 1px inner highlight along the top edge. This is the difference between 'glassy' and 'just translucent' -- translucency alone tends to read as washed out.*
Soft outer glow on the selected tab *Adds a tinted halo. Replaces the rim's shadow, so it includes the rim highlight when both are on.*

Accent bar on the selected tab *A 3px coloured bar down the left edge. The clearest at-a-glance marker if you prefer to keep tints subtle. Uses the same layer as Arc's container glow, so it replaces it.*
Troubleshooting

Outline every element Glassflow touches *Magenta dashed outline on tabs, cyan on window buttons. If something you expected to change has no outline, Glassflow is not matching it and the styling comes from another mod.*
